waiting.title: Accept waitlist wave /w/ links on the invite-code screen
waiting.reporter: Kinjal (kinjaladdanky2.0@gmail.com) by email, Oct 6, 11:57 PM PT, with a screenshot. 78 people hit an “invalid code” on the invite screen in the last 7 days (PostHog). The app doesn't log what they typed, so I can't tell how many of them pasted this link.
waiting.plain: The launch email shows trylatent.co/i/KPCWC4, but tapping-and-holding the link copies a tracking link (trylatent.co/w/…). The invite screen read the tracking bit as the code, turned it into OK2DKWFXHEAQWFR4H99U, and said “That code didn't work.” Now the invite screen recognizes those email links and turns them into the real invite code (KPCWC4). If someone pastes something long that still fails, the error now says the code is the 6 characters at the end of the link. Changes 3 files (+139/−16).
waiting.check: This one you can try yourself. On a signed-out install with the invite screen showing, paste https://trylatent.co/w/5c6d3c19-032b-44b4-9159-71616037df0f/oK2dkWfXH_eaqWFR4H99-U. You should get the green check, not the red error. The agent couldn't run the iOS tests (no Mac on its machine), and CI is off, so run AccessTests on your Mac before merging. The command is in the PR. A new test also fails if the backend's invite link ever stops matching KPCWC4.

waiting.title: Waitlist unsubscribe page shows markup instead of a page
waiting.reporter: Darlen (johnson.darlen2016@gmail.com) by email, Oct 6, 5:23 PM PT: “I think your website to unsubscribe is a little broken.” I confirmed it: Supabase serves that page as plain text, so browsers show the code.
waiting.plain: Every launch email's “unsubscribe here” link opens a Supabase page that shows raw HTML code instead of a confirm button, so people can't easily opt out. That's a spam-complaint and CAN-SPAM risk. With the fix, old links bounce to a new trylatent.co/u/… page (a small Cloudflare Worker) that shows the real confirm page, and new emails link there directly. Email apps' one-click unsubscribe keeps working the same way. 16 new tests pass (12 + 4, run by the agent).
waiting.check: Nothing changes until you deploy, in this order: (1) the Cloudflare Worker (wrangler deploy --config backend/waitlist/unsubscribe-wrangler.toml), then (2) supabase functions deploy unsubscribe. Doing it the other way round gives a 404. After that, open https://wdbggblonxvdbshlaprp.supabase.co/functions/v1/unsubscribe?id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&t=bogus in a browser. It should land on a readable “That link didn't work” page instead of code. Don't test with a real person's link, because that actually unsubscribes them. It's a draft: deploy, check, then mark it ready and merge.
